To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) our method is able to extract explanations with high fidelity from a latent factor recommendation system, (ii) these extracted explanations are able to be used for post hoc explanation of recommendations, (iii) the accuracy of the recommendation system is not compromised by the extraction of these explanations, and (iv) our method is applicable to a range of different recommendation scenarios.
We introduce a novel method for extracting post-hoc explanations from black-box recommendation systems by training an association rule miner on their output.

(1) association rules can be used to extract explanations from latent factor models; (2) the extracted explanations are faithful to the black-box; (3) the explanations can be used to explain the output of a latent factor recommendation system; (4) the extracted explanations can be used for feature engineering in a supervised learning task; and (5) the extracted explanations have a high degree of interpretability
